title: Egyptian Book of the Dead
summary: The Book of the Dead, about 200 funerary spells mostly traceable to the Pyramid Texts and Coffin Texts, first appeared in the early New Kingdom, first on linen shrouds and, by about 1450 BC, on papyrus. It included Spell 125, in which the dead person is judged.

uncertainty.note: Getty: papyrus spells begin "starting around 1550 BCE"; Fitzwilliam: first appeared in the early New Kingdom, on papyrus by about 1450 BC. 1550 BCE = astronomical -1549.

as_recorded.value: By the New Kingdom, starting around 1550 BCE, scribes started writing Book of the Dead spells on papyrus scrolls
first appeared in the early New Kingdom ... By about 1450 BC, they b[ecame papyrus scrolls]

where.modern_name: Luxor, Egypt (proxy: find spot of the shroud of Senneferi named by the Fitzwilliam Museum)
where.historical_name: Thebes region, Egypt, New Kingdom (proxy pin; the sources do not name a place of composition)

importance.justification: A major body of ancient Egyptian funerary spells, including the judgement scene of Spell 125, that evolved over more than 1,000 years per the Getty.

sources.title: What Is the Egyptian Book of the Dead?

reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy: Luxor is where the Fitzwilliam says the Senneferi shroud was found; neither source names where the compilation arose. The earliest date is a rounded "around 1550 BCE" for papyrus; Getty and Fitzwilliam differ slightly (the Getty cites Webennesre papyrus about 1479-1400 BCE).
